  MINUTES
  Regular Meeting of the
  Gardena City Council
  Tuesday, January 10, 2023

  The Regular Meeting Notice and Agenda of the Gardena City Council of the City of Gardena,
  California, was called to order at 7:39 PM on Tuesday, January 10, 2023, in the Council
  Chamber at City Hall 1700 West 162nd Street, Gardena, California; Mayor Tasha Cerda
  presiding.

  1.  ROLL CALL

  Present: Mayor Tasha Cerda; Mayor Pro Tem Paulette C. Francis; Council Member Mark
  E. Henderson; Council Member Rodney G. Tanaka; and Council Member Wanda Love;
  Other City Officials and Employees present: City Manager Clint Osorio; City Attorney
  Carmen Vasquez; City Clerk Mina Semenza; and Deputy City Clerk Becky Romero.

  2.  CLOSED SESSION - None

  PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION - None

  CITY ATTORNEY REPORT OUT OF CLOSED SESSION - None

  3.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Daniel Vasquez and Mariela Vasquez led the Pledge of Allegiance. Both attend Magnolia
  Science Academy 3. Daniel and Mariela are currently in the City of Gardena Teen
  Program. They are long-time participants and have been a part of our afterschool
  programs, youth day camps, and our teen summer and winter programs.

  4.  INVOCATION

  Pastor Nathaniel Session, of Enlightened Ministry Bible Church, gave the Invocation.

  5.  PRESENTATIONS

  5.A  Presentation of the "Holiday Home Decoration Contest 2022" Winners
  - Video presentation was presented.

  Mayor Cerda thanked the Beautification Committee and Chairperson, Mayor
  Pro Tem Francis.

  Mayor Pro Tem Francis thanked everyone who participated in the contest,
  and for making the city look more beautiful during the holidays.

  5.B  Gardena Events Video Presentation
  - Video presentation was presented highlighting the Recreation and Human
  Services Department current and future events.

  Mayor Cerda expressed her appreciation for all the staff and all that they did
  for our residents. She is excited and looks forward to seeing what 2023 is
  going to bring as it relates to events.

  5.  PROCLAMATIONS

  6.A  "Martin Luther King Jr. Celebration Week," January 08 through 16, 2023.
  - Proclamation was accepted by Mayor Pro Tem Ms. Paulette C. Francis,
  Chair of the Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Cultural Committee of Gardena.

  Mayor Pro Tem Francis introduce two committee members Artie Bailey and
  Carrie Scott. She informed everyone that the City of Gardena is the proud
  distinction of being the first city west of Mississippi to honor Dr. King with
  official celebration and the Committee was established by Mr. Arthur
  Johnson in 1972; this is our 50th year; and this is our 40th anniversary. We
  are also one of the few cities that have a two-day Dr. King celebration which
  are our Friday Night Youth Program that takes place on January 13, 2023, at
  the Nakaoka Community Center where the essay contest winners will read
  their essays and be presented with certificates and scholarship award. She
  also announced that the parade was postpone due to weather conditions.
  She thanked the City of Gardena for their continuous support.

  6.  APPOINTMENTS - No Appointments were made

  8.C  CITY TREASURER - Approval of Warrants/Payroll Register, December 27, 2022
  - Item pulled by Mayor Pro Tem Francis

  Mayor Pro Tem Francis asked about the contributions made to the casino for
  Economic assistance resulting from an agreement from a few years ago and asked
  what year it ends. She also asked about the proposed hotel and contingency
  update. City Attorney Vasquez stated that the agreement expires in 2026 and
  explained the agreement requirements.

  It was moved by Mayor Pro Tem Francis, seconded by Council Member
  Tanaka, and carried by the following roll call vote to Approve Item 8.C:

  10. PLANNING & ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY COMMISSION ACTION SHEET

  10.A December 20, 2022 MEETING - Meeting Cancelled

  10.B January 3, 2023 MEETING - Meeting Cancelled

  11. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

  1) Pat Forte, first time attending our Council Meeting; represents a group of people who
  want to help the homeless; spoke about area east of Vermont.

  Mayor Cerda informed Ms. Forte that the area mentioned is not within the City of
  Gardena jurisdiction and asked if she can contact the City Clerk’s office or the City
  Manager’s office so she can get Supervisor Holly Mitchell’s office information and
  possibly see about working with her task force.

  Council Member Tanaka added that he will also provide her with contact information
  for an SBCOG representative for that area.

  2) Sarah Harper, from Mayme Dear Library; came to announce library upcoming events
  happening at the Mayme Dear and Satow Libraries.

  3) Navaline Smith, came out with Pat Forte regarding the homelessness issue.

  12. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES - No Items

  13. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT

  13.A New Bingo License, to conduct bingo games outdoors on the parking lot area of
  the Lucky Lady Casino by the Samoan Congregational Christian Church of South
  Los Angeles

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  4
 DocuSign Envelope ID: B8BEFA7E-8E5F-4DDF-B852-7F147852AD65

  No Public Speakers.

  Council Member Tanaka asked, like the Elks and VFW they do Bingo; what portion
  is the city going to benefit from or is it just the licensing? City Manager Osorio
  confirmed that it is only for licensing.

  Mayor Pro Tem Francis asked where is the bingo going to be played? City
  Manager Osorio confirmed that it will be outside in a tented area of the Lucky Lady
  complex.

  Council Member Love asked if this organization has applied for a bingo permit
  before; has this organization done Bingo before; and is it a church in Gardena or
  they chose the Gardena Casino as a location? City Manager Osorio confirmed that
  the organization has not done any permits or any bingo in the City of Gardena –
  this will be a brand-new application for a new operator. Director of Community
  Development, Greg Tsujiuchi confirmed that the church is not located in Gardena
  and believes that it is in Carson. He also informed everyone that a representative
  from the church was present, and she came up to the podium and made everyone
  aware that the church is in Lomita. Council Member Love also asked how was the
  Lucky Lady chosen? The church representative replied that they wanted to help
  the casino in the City of Gardena by giving back: making donations for back-to-
  school; senior citizens and help the casino as well.

  Mayor Cerda asked about the time and hours of operation; and if they had a
  community meeting with the surrounding homes/neighborhood for feedback? The
  church representative responded that the times and hours are Thursday through
  Sunday from 4:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m. and she also confirmed that a community
  meeting was held.

  It was moved by Council Member Tanaka, seconded by Council Member
  Love, and carried by the following roll call vote to Approve New Bingo
  License:

  Ayes:  Council Members Tanaka and Love, Mayor Pro Tem Francis,
  Council Member Henderson, and Mayor Cerda
  Noes:  None
  Absent: None

  14. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - ELECTED & CITY MANAGER'S OFFICES - No Items

  15. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - POLICE - No Items

  16. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - PUBLIC WORKS

  16.A Authorize the Contract Renewal Services with Smart Cover Systems, Inc. in the
  amount of $31,560 to provide Active Site Management (ASM) and Warranty
  Coverage

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  Council Member Henderson asked about the data that has been collected so far:
  how have we used that data to make wiser decisions; and if the data is not

  5
 DocuSign Envelope ID: B8BEFA7E-8E5F-4DDF-B852-7F147852AD65

  proprietary or a security breaches, can that data be posted on our website for
  transparency. Also, regarding the railroad right-of-way can we get relief from those
  other agencies if there is a backup or do we assume the expense. Director of
  Public Works, Allan Rigg came to the podium and explained the sewer process
  and stated that the data is not proprietary, and he does not know of what value it
  would be if the information was provided to the public since it is only an alert when
  there is a problem. He also explained in depth about the complicated sewer
  system that the city has and since the system has been implemented, we have not
  had one overflow of a public sewer, which is outstanding; he has not seen that in
  any of the cities he has been part of. Director Rigg confirmed that we cannot
  expense the other agency and we must design around their facilities.

  Mayor Pro Tem Francis asked if we are replacing what we have now, because she
  is taking into consideration all the new developments that are currently taking
  place. Also, are we going to get new smart manholes, and do we need to do
  anything else in addition to what we have now to make sure with all the new
  development that our sewers system runs efficiently; does street repairs have any
  affect? Are they covered as part of the maintenance plan, or will it be an additional
  cost? Direct Rigg informed her that the city purchased all the hardware and
  software previously, and this is an extension of the software license that we are
  currently using. As for the new development, they are wrapping up the Sewer
  Master Plan that should be coming out next month and once it is completed it will
  come up with a study of the capacity and conditions of our sewers, it will also
  identify projected development; what sewers will be under capacity, and they will
  look at the possibility of allocating those costs to the new development which is a
  separate effort. He also informed all that manhole stays in place when a street is
  re-done; if the manhole has to be lifted, it is reset and readjusted. He also
  confirmed that it would be an additional cost; we have to incur that cost whether it
  is a smart manhole lid or not.

  Council Member Tanaka asked are some of our sewers shared with the County?
  Director Rigg stated no and explained the 3-part system ownership.

  Council Member Love asked are all our manhole covers smart? What is the
  percentage that are? Are we looking to make them all smart? Do we clean our own
  sewer systems? Can we address the restaurants that are not properly disposing
  their grease?

  Director Rigg replied 30 of 2000 manhole covers are smart; talked about where they
  are located; mentioned that restaurants that don’t properly use their grease traps;
  there are areas within the City where we go and clean up the grease areas. With
  our stormwater permit, we go out and do inspections annually of restaurants if they
  are not properly maintained they are cited; proof that things are running properly is
  that we have had no overflows.

  Mayor Cerda commented and said she was very impressed with the smart manhole
  covers, she was able to go see them in action; she then asked if we get a chance
  we could show the Council the video that she saw because it would put it all into
  perspective.

  16.B Award Construction Contract for the Budlong Avenue from Redondo Beach

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  No public speakers.

  Mayor Pro Tem Francis asked if there is going to be street/traffic lights upgrades;
  and then asked if this is the same company that did Van Ness Avenue. City
  Manager Osorio replied it’s just the street rehab. Director Rigg stated that the
  company that worked on Van Ness project was All American Asphalt, and that we
  have used Sequel Contractor before.

  It was moved by Council Member Henderson, seconded by Council Member

  Contract; Award Construction Management and Inspection Services;
  Approve Budget Appropriation; Approve Project Plans and Specifications;
  and Declare CEQA Exemption:

  Ayes:  Council Members Henderson and Tanaka, Mayor Pro Tem Francis,
  Council Member Love, and Mayor Cerda
  Noes:  None

  16.C Select and Approve the Proposed Conceptual Design to proceed with the
  Construction Document Phase of the Citywide Wayfinding/Entry Sign Program
  Project, JN 507.

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  Public Works Director Allan Rigg was gave a PowerPoint presentation.

  After the presentation, Council gave their input and recommendations; Director
  Rigg answered all questions. Mayor Cerda recommended we start with a policy
  about which signs we replace first. Five different designs were presented and each
  of the Council Members chose one each of the five designs. City Manager

  A member from the public, Ms. Phillips, came up to the podium and gave her
  recommendation, and chose design number 3.

  Council came to a consensus and chose design number 3 and chose the fancier

  22. COUNCIL REMARKS

  1) COUNCIL MEMBER HENDERSON – Council Member Henderson wished everyone a
  Happy New Year. Since the last meeting Council Member Henderson attended the
  SCAG meeting and Regional SCAG meeting as he represents the City of Gardena.
  Council Member Henderson will be attending a SCAG meeting on January 19th as he is
  chairing the Racial Equity and Housing Committee. He also shared the Southern
  California Area of Governments will be presenting at the next Council Meeting. Council
  Member Henderson thanked the City Manager, City Staff, and Department Heads for
  listening to their concerns in wanting to improve the city.

  2) MAYOR PRO TEM FRANCIS – Since the last meeting Mayor Pro Tem Francis
  attended the Greater Los Angeles County Vector Control District meeting, and
  Beautification Commission meeting. Mayor Pro Tem Francis attended Shop with a Cop
  and thanked the Gardena Police Department for their generosity in paying for the
  children’s toys out of their own money. She also attended the toy giveaway hosted by
  the Helping Hands Program, and flag football awards banquet. Mayor Pro Tem Francis
  shared the Martin Luther King Jr. commemoration program will be on January 13th

  3) COUNCIL MEMBER TANAKA – Since the last meeting Council Member Tanaka
  attended the Finance Committee meeting, SBCOG Homeless Task force meeting,
  League of California Cities meeting, South Bay Aerospace Alliance meeting, DCS
  check in, and happy dance toy giveaway. Council Member Tanaka shared he tried to
  attend every event Director Santin hosted before the new year. Apologized for not
  attending the PD Toy Giveaway but heard positive feedback. Council Member Tanaka
  shared he had the privilege of working with those listed in the remembrances and Mrs.
  Rocha she was a great community leader that did a lot of nonprofit work for the city.

  4) MAYOR CERDA – Mayor Cerda tried to attend all the events before the new year.
  Mayor Cerda attended Jolley Trolley, Shop with a Cop, Acts of Kindness, and
  Christmas parties. Mayor Cerda thanked all the departments for organizing and
  working together. Since the last meeting Mayor Cerda attended the swearing in of the
  City of Long Beach Mayor Rex Richardson, and event for Sydney Kamlager, who is
  going to Congress. Lastly, wished Minnie Thomas a Gardena resident a Happy
  Birthday as she turned 100 years old.

  5) COUNCIL MEMBER LOVE – Council Member Love wished everyone a happy new
  year. Since the last Council Meeting Council Member Love attended Let’s Talk Trash
  event with WRG. Council Member Love was unable to attend Shop with a Cop event
  because she hosted a toy giveaway with one of the businesses in the city. Council
  Member Love shared the Chamber of Commerce hosted the Christmas Day luncheon
  and gave a shout out to PD and the POA as they helped sponsored the event. She
  also shared that during the toy giveaway the kids had a lot of fun, and she was very
  happy that the police officers were engaging with the children. Lastly, thanked Director
  Riggs and Director Crespo for working on adding light to one of the bus stops and for
  trimming the tree.

  24. REMEMBRANCES

  Mr. Don Pastel, former police officer with the Gardena Police Department;
